Name: Start
Line: Oh — hello dear. Are you the one who's come to get me ready? My mother is visiting today, I need to look my best.
Notes: DRAFT - for SC&H review. Opening beat; Maria believes her late mother is visiting.

Name: Greet
Line: She's bringing lemon cake. She always does, on Saturdays.
Option1Text: That sounds lovely, Maria. Tell me about your mother.
Option2Text: Maria, it's Tuesday today — and your mother passed away some years ago.
Option3Text: Let's get you ready then. Shall we pick out a cardigan?
Notes: DRAFT. First choice point: three core techniques.

Name: Validate_1
Line: Oh, she's wonderful. She wears a blue coat, and she sings while she bakes. You'd like her, I think.
Option1Text: She sounds kind — just like you. What do you sing together?
Option2Text: It's nice remembering her, isn't it? Let's sit by the window while we chat.
Notes: DRAFT. Validation path deepens; Maria at ease.

Name: Validate_2
Line: We sing 'You Are My Sunshine'. She holds my hand at the chorus... Oh, I do miss her hand.
Option1Text: You must love her very much. I'm glad you told me.
Option2Text: Would you like to sing it together while I tidy the room?
Notes: DRAFT. Emotional truth acknowledged without correcting the delusion; she settles.

Name: Confront_1
Line: What? No... no, that's not right. She was just here. Why would you say something so horrible?
Option1Text: I'm sorry, Maria. That was upsetting. You were telling me about the lemon cake?
Option2Text: I'm only telling you the truth. It's important you understand.
Notes: DRAFT. Reality orientation backfires - distress. Student can repair or double down.

Name: Confront_2
Line: Stop it! I want you to leave. Where's my mother? MOTHER?
Option1Text: I'm sorry. I'll sit quietly with you for a moment.
Option2Text: I'll fetch the nurse and give you some space.
Notes: DRAFT. Escalation peak; only de-escalation exits.

Name: Repair_1
Line: ...She really does make the best lemon cake. You believe me, don't you?
Option1Text: I believe the cake is wonderful. Saturdays with her sound special.
Option2Text: Of course. Shall we get you comfortable while you tell me more?
Notes: DRAFT. Repair path; trust partially restored if validated.

Name: Redirect_1
Line: A cardigan... yes. The green one, mother likes me in green. Is it cold out today?
Option1Text: A little cool. The green one it is — it brings out your eyes.
Option2Text: It's mild. Maria, do you remember what day it is today?
Notes: DRAFT. Redirection partial success; quizzing is a common student error.

Name: Quiz_1
Line: Day? It's... Saturday? No — you're testing me. Everyone keeps testing me.
Option1Text: I'm sorry, it doesn't matter. The green cardigan, you said?
Option2Text: I'm not testing you. It's Tuesday. Your mother isn't coming.
Notes: DRAFT. Orientation quizzing causes anxiety - teachable moment.

Name: Redirect_2
Line: You're gentle, aren't you. Most of them rush me. Sit a moment — the light is nice this time of morning.
Option2Text: Of course — and I'll open the curtains a little wider for you.
Notes: DRAFT. Converging calm beat before close; both options are appropriate closes with different technique tags.

Name: Close_Warm
Line: Thank you, dear. When my mother arrives... well. Perhaps it's enough that you listened.
Notes: DRAFT. Warm end state. Moment of lucidity left deliberately ambiguous.

Name: Close_Distress
Line: (Maria turns to the window, hands working at her blanket. The visit is over.)
Notes: DRAFT. Distress end state - no audio; stage direction as subtitle. Debrief should flag this outcome.
